title: Modelling quantum measurement dynamics: from decoherence to redundancy with site-hopping indistinguishable particles
authors: Katja Schneeweiss, Tom Rivlin, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Marcus Huber, Iva Březinová
abstract: In recent years, new theoretical insights into decoherence and quantum measurements have emerged through the study of many-body dynamics in isolated quantum systems. It is now understood that the parameters and energy scales in system-environment interactions decisively affect how readily information spreads from a quantum system into its surroundings during a decoherence event. A popular choice for studying these effects is the framework of quantum Darwinism (QD), but so far few works have applied this to realistic many-body models. Inspired by experimentally-accessible setups, in this work we introduce a simple, flexible, numerically exact many-body model of a system broadcasting information into an environment: a 1D lattice of sites with hopping particles. We show that different choices of parameters lead to the recovery of known scenarios featuring different decoherence and QD effects, such as equilibration, revivals of coherence, and redundancy. In constructing this model we resolve the crucial issue of indistinguishability: we explain how to calculate the entropy of a fraction of the environment when said environment is composed of indistinguishable fermions or bosons (or lattice sites containing them). We then show that particle statistics can make a notable difference to the QD properties of the setup, with fermionic environments sometimes achieving redundancy much more readily than bosonic or site-based ones. Our work opens the door to much closer alignment between theoretical models and experimental tests of the dynamics of quantum measurements and the quantum-to-classical transition.
summary: This paper develops and analyzes a flexible many-body model—a 1D lattice with hopping indistinguishable particles—to study how quantum measurement dynamics proceed from decoherence toward classical redundancy. By incorporating particle statistics (fermions vs. bosons), the authors demonstrate that these fundamental details significantly alter the emergence of objective information, providing crucial theoretical alignment for future experiments using ultracold atoms.
main_problem: The paper models quantum measurement dynamics, specifically investigating the transition from decoherence to redundancy within the framework of Quantum Darwinism (QD) using realistic many-body systems.
main_result: Particle statistics significantly impact QD properties, showing that fermionic environments can achieve information redundancy more readily than bosonic or site-based ones. The model successfully reproduces known decoherence dynamics by tuning parameters.
method: The authors use numerically exact time evolution simulations on a 1D lattice to calculate quantum observables like Quantum Mutual Information (QMI) and environmental entropy.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D lattice containing an impurity particle interacting with an environment composed of indistinguishable hopping particles (fermions or hard-core bosons). The Hamiltonian includes terms for environment hopping ($\hat{H}_E$) and interaction between the impurity and environment ($\hat{H}_{IE}$).
key_observables: Quantum Mutual Information (QMI), decoherence parameter $D(t)$, environmental entropy, and indicators of classicality like equilibration and redundancy.
important_parameters: $W_{EE}$ (environment interaction strength), $W_{IE}$ (impurity-environment coupling), and the particle statistics (fermionic vs. bosonic).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that measurements must be performed at times when the decoherence parameter $D(t) \approx 0$ for a fair QMI assessment, and it simplifies by setting $\hat{H}_I = 0$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of QMI showing the loss of an initial 'redundancy plateau' due to environment-environment interactions. They also show how revival characteristics decrease with increasing system size.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the model, details methods for handling indistinguishable particles in environmental entropy calculations, analyzes the effect of particle statistics on QD properties via QMI measurements over time, and discusses the implications for aligning theory with experiments.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental questions about quantum-to-classical transition using a highly tunable model inspired by ultracold atom simulators, making it highly relevant to AMO physics research in open quantum systems.
